messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — after the kernel-steering tweak pushed last night, we're seeing a spike in eval deltas for quantized workloads. +6.1% hallucination rate on our structured-output eval set. cc @Jia @Sam
Jia Patel: Which canary/commit? I assume the steering switch that prefers FP8 kernels for short sequences?
Alex Chen: yes — canary id 2247652, commit d9a3b1f. Canary shows kernel steering prefers fp8_fast when seq_len < 128, but telemetry shows an increased INT8 fallback rate for longctx shards.
Sam Rodriguez: Perf slice from canary: p50 ~ +4ms, p95 +22ms, p99 +35ms. Throughput down ~11% on mix-quant profile. Fallbacks: 23% of requests triggered fp8->int8 path; KV cache hit-rate for those requests dropped from 91% -> 68%.
Michael O'Neil: That KV-hit drop smells like schema/version mismatch in cached KV keys when kernel path flips. Could be dtype/packing change between kernels.
Jia Patel: I pulled a sample request trace:
```
TRACE id=abc123
models: redwood-mix-v2 -> kernel=fp8_fast -> fallback=int8_pref
kv_cache_keys: [layer_3:hash(0x830a), layer_6:hash(0x12b4)]
cached_dtype: uint8
runtime_dtype: int8
```
Looks like the cache encoding differs when fp8_fast runs vs int8_pref.
Alex Chen: eval-bot reported example with broken JSON output for a schema'd assistant response. Instead of {"answer": {"text":...}} we got {"answer_text": "..."} — downstream parsers fail and product SLOs hit. Posting sample:
```
EXPECTED: {"answer": {"text": "42", "source": "wiki"}}
OBSERVED: {"answer_text": "42|wiki"}
```
Sam Rodriguez: That's the structured-output regression. Our hypothesis: quantized kernel alters tokenization or stops tokens earlier due to calibration shift -> special token sequences (separator chars) get merged.
Michael O'Neil: We need repro that ties kernel switch -> cache mismatch -> altered logits -> early stop / token merge. I can instrument the canary runtime to dump raw logits + kv_serialization on fallback path.
ci-bot: Deployed canary 2247652 -> rollback window ends 1767661000.
Jia Patel: Running a small manual repro now with the example prompt. Repro steps: 1) run canary with force-kernel=fp8_fast, 2) hit with prompt batch 1000 w/ seq distribution, 3) compare token-level logits and decode path.
Alex Chen: Quick diff of two decodes (fp8_fast vs pure-fp32):
fp32 decode: ["<s>", "answer", ":", " ", "42", "</s>"]
fp8_fast decode: ["<s>", "answer_text", ":", " ", "42|wiki", "</s>"]
Notice tokenization boundary after 'answer' differs.
Sam Rodriguez: Telemetry snippets:
- eval-set EM delta: -5.2
- hallucination rate: +6.1%
- json-parse-errors in prod: +0.8%
These correlate with increased fallback ratio and KV miss rate.
Michael O'Neil: Hypothesis: fp8 kernel uses a different calibration table that slightly shifts logits near special-token boundaries; when fallback to int8 happens mid-request, KV cache re-insertion uses the fp8-encoded keys, consumer reads as int8 -> mismatch.
Jia Patel: Proposed mitigations: 1) Force consistent KV serialization dtype across kernels, 2) Pin kernel steering to avoid mid-request kernel path flips, 3) Re-run calibration with edge tokens baked into calibration set.
Alex Chen: For immediate mitigation I recommend disabling steering for the mixed-quant model on canary and aborting rollout. Sam, can you flip steering flag and rerun the eval harness?
Sam Rodriguez: On it — toggling steering=false for canary now. Also kicking off a smoke run: 2k requests with our structured-output prompt set.
(eval-bot): Quick eval result (after steering disable): EM delta reduced to -0.9, hallucination +1.2%, json errors back to baseline. Full run pending.
Jia Patel: Good. For a durable fix: we should add a runtime invariant check that refuses to serve fallback if the KV serialization format would differ. Also add calibration samples that include our structured delim tokens and JSON punctuation.
Michael O'Neil: I'll open a runtime PR to add a serialization-version header to KV entries and validate on read. Also will add a flag to forbid mid-request kernel switches when any cached entries exist.
Alex Chen: Please include a perf test — the serialization header must be tiny (<8B) to not regress throughput. Sam, add a microbenchmark in the batching harness for serialization overhead.
Sam Rodriguez: Will do. Early timeline: hotfix (steering off) done; runtime KV header + kernel-swap guard PR by EOD; calibration re-run + canary next week.
Alex Chen: Thanks team. Keep this thread updated with repro artifacts (raw logits, kv-hex dumps, eval diffs). Ping me if canary shows any other anomalies. :thumbsup:
Jia Patel: Uploaded kv-hex dump to /internal/hunts/2247652/kv_dump_1.bin and linked to the trace.
Michael O'Neil: Adding unit tests for serialization + a util to migrate existing caches (small script).
Sam Rodriguez: Note: watch for p99 latency once header lands — serialization validation is sync on read. Might need async validation + background migration.
Alex Chen: Agreed. We'll prioritize correctness first, then iterate on async migration to recover latency.
(eval-bot): Full eval complete: hallucination delta now +0.6 (after rollback), structured-output parse errors back to baseline. Closing canary for now.
